title: Distinguish different sensorimotor performance of the hand between the individuals with diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease through deep learning models
summary: Full primary paper uses CNNs to classify hand sensorimotor performance across controls, diabetes and CKD using retrospective data; no causal or clinical benefit claim. Internal train/validation/test splits; retrospective group discrimination only.
ai_technology: Deep learning classifies sensorimotor task patterns from hand-task measurements.
organization: College of Engineering; National Cheng Kung University

evidence.tested: Retrospective data: 75 controls, 159 DM and 37 CKD; reported inter-participant accuracies ~.88–.90 and AUC up to .977.
evidence.unknown: Internal train/validation/test splits; retrospective group discrimination only. The source does not establish benefits beyond the reported evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning classifies sensorimotor task patterns from hand-task measurements.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
